extracted.intended_audience: attorneys authorized to practice before the USPTO, Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and parties in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal-discipline proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for imposing and implementing reciprocal discipline against a practitioner before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including notice, response period, suspension scope/duration, publication, account restrictions, duties during suspension, and reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may file a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline requesting that the Director of the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline upon a respondent identical to the discipline imposed by a state court or authority, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complaint seeks imposition of discipline identical to the state order; the Notice and Order must identify the grounds for imposing reciprocal discipline and reference the applicable provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Order service and response period
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' must be sent (here by certified mail) notifying the respondent of the Complaint and providing an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service by certified mail (with receipt) to the address where the OED reasonably believes the respondent receives mail; the Notice must advise the respondent of the 40-day deadline and the bases listed in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1) on which they may oppose imposition of identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond: no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file a response to the Notice and Order within the prescribed period, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and proceed to impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-response permits the OED to treat the facts as uncontested for purposes of § 11.24(d) and to apply the identical discipline unless a statutory exception in § 11.24(d) is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of suspension identical to state order
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline imposed by the USPTO is identical in substance and duration to the discipline ordered by the state; in this case, suspension for six (6) months and one (1) day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO imposes the same sanction as the imposing state authority (subject to the regulatory framework of § 11.24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of suspension — trademark and non-patent practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension may be limited in scope (e.g., the respondent is suspended from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order clarifies scope (here: trademark and non-patent matters) and may note the respondent's existing authorization status in patent matters (e.g., not authorized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and reinstatement — petition under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 required
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent remains suspended until the OED Director grants a petition requesting reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is not automatic at the end of the state-imposed period unless a petition under § 11.60 is filed and granted by the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties during suspension — compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Final Order cites § 11.58, the specific duties (e.g., client notification, file transfer, withdrawal procedures) are set forth in that regulation and must be followed by the suspended practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order includes sample notice language to be used in the Official Gazette; disciplinary decisions are made available for public review via the OED FOIA Reading Room URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts — 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for it to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures other jurisdictions and relevant courts are informed of the USPTO action and the underlying reasons for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to USPTO verified Electronic System accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO verified Electronic System account, shall not obtain such an account, nor shall he have his name added to a USPTO verified Electronic System account, unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute prohibition (during suspension) on initiating or being listed on verified USPTO accounts used for filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using or assisting in use of USPTO.gov accounts for filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is prohibited from using, accessing, or assisting others in using or accessing any USPTO.gov account(s) or other USPTO filing systems for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO unless and until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition expressly covers assisting others, not just the respondent's personal use.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO authorized to disallow specified account activities until reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Until reinstatement, the USPTO is authorized to disallow the respondent from: (1) opening or activating any USPTO.gov account(s) used for preparing or filing documents; (2) applying for any such account(s); (3) verifying any other person's credentials in connection with such accounts; and (4) sponsoring any USPTO.gov account(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates concrete account-related actions that the USPTO may block; these are independent prohibitions the respondent may not attempt while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: No obligation on USPTO to reactivate disabled accounts sua sponte
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO is not obligated to take action sua sponte to re-activate any USPTO.gov account disabled or suspended pursuant to the order; it is the respondent's sole responsibility to initiate any such re-activation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that reactivation requires affirmative action by the respondent (e.g., petition/requests) rather than automatic reinstatement by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for reciprocal discipline — underlying state misconduct (criminal plea/family-law-related misconduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal action may be predicated upon the respondent's suspension in a state court based on misconduct (here: a guilty plea to misdemeanor harassment and interference with judicial proceedings arising from actions during family law proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order describes the factual basis of the state discipline to show the predicate misconduct for USPTO reciprocal discipline; such misconduct can form the factual basis for imposing reciprocal sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for USPTO disciplinary action — 35 U.S.C. § 32
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action by the USPTO is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and implementing regulations such as 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites the federal statutory authority supporting USPTO disciplinary procedures and reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service requirements for Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order must be mailed (here by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested) to the respondent at the address where the OED Director reasonably believes the respondent receives mail, and a certificate of service documenting mailing is included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service is required to support the proceeding and to trigger response deadlines; the Final Order includes a signed certificate of service with recipient address.
